# Probing Deferred Commitments in Language Agents with Counterfactual Replays

Ilse Marwedel, Kofi Brandtner, Sunniva Okafor-Lund

Abstract:

Language agents often settle on a course of action several steps before they act on it, and the moment of that commitment is rarely visible in their transcripts. We introduce counterfactual replays, which re-run an agent from a saved state with one observation altered, and use the point at which alterations stop changing the final action as an estimate of when the agent committed. Across three task suites and five agent scaffolds, commitments arrive on average four steps before the action they determine, and earlier for agents that plan in writing. Replays also reveal a minority of episodes in which the stated plan and the estimated commitment disagree, which we argue are the episodes most worth reading by hand.

Comments: 14 pages, 6 figures; code at https://example.org/replays

Subjects: Machine Learning (ex.LG); Artificial Intelligence (ex.AI)
